sn52.8:1.1: _Salaḷa_ is usually identified with frankincense (variant _sallakī_, Sanskrit _śallakī_, *Boswellia serrata*), but this is uncertain. Frankincense thrives in arid highlands quite distant from the rich riverlands of Sāvatthī, and is a straggly tree unsuited to construction (although the hut could simply be near a frankincense). The Apadāna refers to flowers or garlands of _salaḷa_ ([tha-ap209](), [tha-ap212:11.4](), [tha-ap556:3.3)), but the frankincense flower is small and a poor candidate for garlands.[mn93:11.6]() and [mn96:16.3]() speak of the fire from the _salaḷa_. Taken together these references suggest that a variety of frankincense tree is likely to be not too far off. Such trees, however, are fairly straggly, barely more than shrubs, and I don’t think could serve as timber. Perhaps it was used for wattle-and-daub, or else the hut was simply near the tree.
sn52.8:3.3: BB mistakenly inserts “give up the training” here and in the parallel passage at SN 35.244. At SN 45.160, he correctly omits it.
